# Horizon's Java regex vendor

This directory vendors `java_regex` 0.1.0, originally authored by Mathieu Dutour Sikiric, from the locally cached crates.io release. Upstream: <https://github.com/MathieuDutSik/java_regex>. Crates.io archive SHA-256: `1f3b3ff81a66205722b636dae12fc5cb2e77147569e8968f38a1d73b2b05fbe6`. Original MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses and accompanying documentation remain included. The local manifest omits upstream benchmark/differential-driver dependencies; this is an isolated workspace for focused compatibility tests.

Local changes are derived from execution and bytecode inspection of the pinned Java 25 reference, not from another Minecraft client or mod:

- Separate `Pattern.single` literal/Single-class comparison from symmetric case-insensitive back-reference comparison. Java's Unicode literal comparison is directional: `(?iu)ß` does not match `ẞ`, whereas `(?iu)ẞ` matches `ß`.
- Preserve numeric Unicode/surrogate endpoints in character classes. A valid Java range such as `[a-\x{D800}]` must compile; an unpaired surrogate does not become a NUL literal.
- Replace the simplified `\X` matcher with pinned `unicode-segmentation` 1.12.0 (Unicode 16). Java 25 oracle cases cover Hangul L/V/T, Indic conjuncts, Prepend, SpacingMark, CRLF, emoji ZWJ with Extend, RI triples, and control/combining boundaries.
- Java Character predicate flags use compact Unicode 16 ranges regenerated by `tools/regex_reference/JavaPropertyRanges.java` (~42 KB of runtime triples). This replaces Rust-toolchain-dependent character properties, approximate mirroring/identifier checks, and covers the six Java emoji predicates.
- Simple case-mapping data is regenerated by `tools/regex_reference/JavaCaseMappings.java` against Java 25 (Unicode 16). These are character-mapping observations, not copied JDK implementation code.

Literal runs preserve Java SliceU behavior separately from SingleU: `(?iu)ßx` matches `ẞx`, while a captured or quantified standalone ß remains exact. Unicode class ranges and grapheme-boundary anchors are also covered by Java reference cases.

Run the focused tests with `cargo test --manifest-path third_party/java_regex/Cargo.toml --test horizon`. Private Java matrix tests are ignored by default and accept `HORIZON_JAVA_REGEX_ORACLE`.

The upstream compatibility claims in its README are retained as upstream documentation, not as a Horizon claim that all Java Pattern behavior has been verified. The pinned grapheme cases are verified, while exhaustive Unicode-property coverage and other undocumented engine quirks remain subject to differential checks against the pinned JDK.

## Native stack growth

The optional `stack-growth` feature uses `stacker` at both node and quantifier recursion entries (64 KiB red zone, 1 MiB segments). It disables upstream's artificial 500-frame / five-million-step false-result cutoffs; a valid Java match is not changed into a non-match because it crosses those counters. The default no_std feature set retains upstream's bounded behavior. Enable `stack-growth` for Horizon's native policy evaluator. This is stack allocation support, not a timeout or a different pattern language; trusted local patterns retain Java-like unbounded backtracking behavior. The upstream catastrophic-backtracking limit test runs only in the bounded default configuration.

## Unicode blocks and version pins

`java_blocks.rs` contains Java 25 `UnicodeBlock.of` intervals and exact aliases verified with public `UnicodeBlock.forName`. `tools/regex_reference/JavaBlockRanges.java` regenerates them from reflected public fields plus Unicode 16 UCD Blocks.txt canonical display-name candidates; every candidate is passed through the JDK before inclusion. Lookup uppercases names without stripping punctuation or whitespace. Thus `TULU_TIGALARI` and `Tulu-Tigalari` are valid, while `TuluTigalari` is rejected exactly as Java does. The legacy `SURROGATES_AREA` alias remains valid with no matching intervals. Block membership includes unassigned code points inside a block, independently of Character.isDefined.

`unicode-script` is pinned to 0.5.7 and `unicode-general-category` to 1.1.0 for Unicode 16. The Unicode 17 block dependency and unused unicode-properties dependency have been removed. The generated block data has 338 intervals and 782 verified aliases (~15 KB of name text, plus interval/index storage); Unicode 17-only names such as Beria Erfe and Tai Yo are not admitted.

## Named-character lexer integration

`Regex::new_with_name_resolver(pattern, fn(&str) -> Option<u32>)` accepts the caller's strict Java Character name lookup. `\N{...}` is parsed at the lexer, both outside and inside classes, so quoted or commented text is never preprocessed. The resolver receives raw name contents and may return surrogate code points. Unknown names, missing braces, and other reserved unsupported ASCII-letter escapes are compilation errors; escaped non-ASCII literals remain allowed. Numeric class back-references and a bare `\0` remain invalid, while an undefined numeric back-reference outside a class compiles and never matches, as Java does.

Explicit repetition counts are limited to Java's signed 32-bit range. Java 25 accepts 2,147,483,647 but rejects larger decimal minimum/maximum counts; parsing them as Rust u32 must not admit invalid policy expressions.
